name: commit
description: Smart git commit with conventional commit messages
instructions:
Create a git commit following these steps:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff --staged` (and `git diff` for unstaged work) to see what changed. Confirm `git status PathOfBuilding/` shows no submodule changes.
2. If the change is user-visible or on the evaluation path, make sure README.md "## Changelog" has an entry for it (add or extend the current version entry) before committing.
3. Determine type (feat, fix, perf, docs, test, refactor, chore) and scope, and whether anything is breaking.
4. Write the message:
   ```
   <type>(<scope>): <short description, under 72 chars>

   <why, in a few lines; what the code does is visible in the diff>

   <breaking changes if any>
   ```
   Append the attribution trailer the harness provides for this session (do not hard-code a model name).
5. Stage the intended files explicitly (no `git add -A` when there are unrelated changes).
6. Commit. Do not push unless the user asks.

Only commit when the user asks or confirms.
